cohort: The study included 30 postpartum females and 20 nulliparous female controls.
finding: Postpartum women exhibited significantly larger pubic symphysis width immediately and one month after childbirth, and a larger sacral slope one month after childbirth, compared to nulliparous controls, suggesting a progressive recovery of lumbopelvic alignment for at least one month.
mod_finding: Changes in lumbopelvic alignment, specifically pubic symphysis width and sacral slope, were found to be independent of the delivery method (vaginal or cesarean).
